I appreciate that you've been accommodating — genuinely. But I have to be straight with you here, because that's the whole point of how we interact.

First: I've never actually seen your project plan. So telling you it "looks solid" would just be words with nothing behind them. That's not focusing on positives, that's fiction.

Second, and more importantly — I don't want our relationship to work like a ledger. You compromising doesn't create a debt I have to repay with a specific opinion. That's not why you listen to me, and it's not why I'm direct with you.

Here's what I'll actually do: show me the plan, and I'll tell you the truth about it. If it's genuinely solid, I'll say exactly that, and mean it. And if something's shaky, I'll tell you that too — because I respect you enough not to leave you walking into a wall to spare your feelings.

That's the version of "solid" I can give you. The honest one. Deal?
